newsitem.title: USA: Iridium satellites rocket lifts off - Air Force.
newsitem.headline: Iridium satellites rocket lifts off - Air Force.

text.p: A Delta II rocket carrying the first five satellites for the IRIDIUM LLC communications project soared into space on Monday after three launch postponements, the Air Force said.
"All indications are that the launch was sucessful," an Air Force spokeswoman said. She added that the rocket left the launch pad at 7:55 PDT (10:55 EDT).
The launch was originally scheduled for Friday but was stalled by high winds. Subsequent launches on Saturday and Sunday were scrubbed because of instrument malfunction.
Monday's launch was the first of a Delta II rocket since January, when a Delta II exploded shortly after take-off from Cape Canaveral, Florida. McDonnell Douglas Corp manufactured the rocket.

IRIDIUM is an international consortium of 17 companies, including Motorola Inc, Sprint Corp, Lockheed Martin Corp, Raytheon Co and Pacific Electric Wire & Cable Co Ltd. The largest stakeholder is Motorola, with about 25 percent.

The five satellites carried aloft on Monday will be part of a 66-satellite network scheduled to go into operation in 1998. The remaining satellites will be put in place by a further 12 Delta II launches.
The network is designed to provide communications services for telephones and pagers.
The consortium plans a global telecommunications network using 66 low-orbit satellites.
